subject: design/maintenance-sweep-v1
statement: The pass emits exactly one report per invocation: the **machine face** — one JSON object of a new closed, versioned schema (report + finding elements; the schema is the shape's) — on stdout; the **human face** on stderr (#D-2). Findings carry the PRD's four fields (detector, subject, evidence, remedy — prd FR-1); applied waivers are surfaced with their reasons (prd FR-10); a faulted detector appears as a named fault inside the report (prd UB-3). The **exit ranking is pinned**: any finding emitted → exit **1** (a coexisting detector fault stays named inside the report, never silently absorbed — the findings are the pass's actionable product); zero findings with any fault — pass-level (usage, misparse, unreadable state, malformed policy) or detector-level — → exit **2**; zero findings, zero faults → exit **0**; the machine face's `outcome` field maps by the same ranking (findings > fault > clean). The **human face is explicit on emptiness**: each clean detector prints its explicit "0 findings" line — never silence (the PRD's F1 empty state, held in this frozen half). The report pins the evaluated state honestly: `evaluated_state.commit` names HEAD, and a non-clean working tree sets a named `dirty` annotation on the machine face plus a human-face warning — the commit then names the base of the evaluated tree, not its exact bytes; the §3.7 correlation claim and every live bar run on clean checkouts (AP-13's clean-tree corollary). Ordering is fixed (detector order, then lexicographic subjects), and no machine-face field carries wall-clock content — the report is the event record (prd EVT-1) and a regenerable projection of state (the AP-28 posture the PRD states).
